newsitem.title: INDIA: India gold, silver down on stock sales,poor demand.
newsitem.headline: India gold, silver down on stock sales,poor demand.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) closes 95 rupees lower at 7,555 rupees per kg on heavy selling by stockists following sharp losses in world markets.
** Gold 24 carat closes 55 rupees lower at 4,895 rupees per 10 gramme amid sluggish seasonal buying. Reports of a setback in world markets prompt profit-taking.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) closed 700 rupees lower at 57,300 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) closed 95 rupees lower at 7,555 rupees per kg on increased selling by stockists following reports of setback in world markets, dealers said.
Silver was down 10 rupees per kg on Tuesday but was up by 15 rupees on Monday. It was up 95 rupees last week.
"Demand resistance from industrial buyers also dragged prices lower today as they kept on the sidelines expecting further price erosion," one dealer said.
Gold 24 carat closed 55 rupees lower at 4,895 rupees per 10 gramme as seasonal buying petered out and stockists chose to book profits following reports of losses in world markets.
Prices of gold biscuit (116.50 gramme each) closed 700 rupees lower at 57,300 rupees per piece, dealers said. They were steady on Tuesday but were down by 200 rupees on Monday.
Gold biscuit prices were up 1,200 rupees per piece last week. Fresh arrivals of imported gold remained low but supplies were good on resumption of sale of confiscated gold by the customs department.
